Although I was not to know it was this message was passed to UKLF --" The U.K. Land Forces. "-- MOD, FCO and thence to Geneva where Lord Owen used it to browbeat Boban, the HVO Military Commander there." In conjunction with that document, General, I'd like to turn to a document that we just need to go briefly into private section with, Mr. President, and that would be 406/45, which is another UN document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, all right. I hope it will be very brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it is 406/45. I apologise. (Private session)

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, was it the conclusion of the HVO military authorities and of the HVO political authorities that land that they secured militarily will ultimately be granted to them under the Vance-Owen Peace Plan? Are you aware of that thinking?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know what my obligations were in terms of the Vance-Owen Plan if all signed it, related to demobilisation activities and activities related to the establishment of a joint command. As for a plan concerning the military implementation of the Vance-Owen Plan, I am not aware of that. I also wish to note that throughout this time that we're talking about, convoys with military equipment were passing through Kiseljak and going to Visoko --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, I'm sorry to interrupt you but I have to move on. Now, General, let me show you the next document, if I could, which is an another military information summary.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 676.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is a situation report, again for Busovaca, on the 25th of January, 1993, general. "The situation in the Busovaca/Kacuni area has deteriorated dramatically in the last twenty four hours since the initial exchange of fire at the BiH checkpoint outside Kacuni. At 0650 hours this morning a callsign reported that the main road at grid reference," and it gives a grid reference, "was blocked with two trucks with landmines placed beneath them. At 0730 hours the Dutch transport battalion reported that fighting had broken out in the southern edge of town. Information later received led them to believe that HVO soldiers were forcibly entering Muslim houses in search of members of the BiH army. A Warrior callsign reported that they were unable to proceed through the HVO checkpoint," with a grid reference, "due to small-arms fire south of the checkpoint. The commanding officer left this location at 1115 hours and married up with the callsign at the checkpoint and proceeded towards Busovaca. At 1150 hours, artillery rounds were reported to be landing to the north of Kacuni and at grid reference," and it gives a grid reference. "There was a BiH lorry blocking the road. The BiH soldiers initially would not allow the UN vehicles to pass through until an order was passed down from 3 Corps headquarters. The CO," commanding officers, "continued on to Kiseljak leaving two Warrior callsigns on the main road," and it gives the grid reference. "At 1125 hours this morning, 3 Corps headquarters stated that the village of Dusina at grid reference had many civilian casualties and could we assist in evacuating them back to Zenica. Comment. Is believed that the village of Dusina was predominately Muslim and was shelled from HVO positions in the Busovaca area. Comment ends. "The commanding officer, on returning through Busovaca, reported seeing approximately twenty houses burning in Busovaca. Comment. Commanding officer believed that this was a clear example of the HVO ethnically cleansing Muslims from the town. Comment ends. It was reported that the Muslims have agreed to a cease-fire starting at 0600 hours tomorrow morning." It talks about tensions and gives a list of checkpoints. If we go to the next page at the comment. Can you move it up a little bit, Mr. Usher? "Comment. Several of the houses around the two checkpoints in Kacuni were reported to be burning. It is believed these houses may have belonged to Croats. The occupants have been ethnically cleansed probably by the Bosnian army. The threat to any vehicles travelling on this road is still high and remains close to soft-skinned vehicles. This means that both our main supply routes are currently closed. However, that is detour suitable for non-track vehicles around Busovaca." Now, General, this is the outset of the conflict in Busovaca and Kacuni; is it not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This was quite long. You said that this -- whether this was the outset of the conflict. During the day, the 25th, I received information that during the night, during the second half of the night, that is to say, at 0100 on the 25th, at the checkpoint of the BH army in Kacuni or that barricade, a member of the military police of the HVO was killed, and a civilian as well, and that this led to further activity. As for the roadblock on the main road, that is to say, the two trucks, I think that one of the Prosecution witnesses spoke about this. He was stopped at that road. These trucks had logs on them, they were prepared for a roadblock, and one of them, on the 10th of August, when an attempt was made at liquidation, it went after me at the same barricade. At this time that you were reading about, that is to say, the 25th of January, 1993, I did not have any knowledge thereof in the morning, and I left my house of birth towards Kacuni, towards the point of conflict, and I was moving towards the headquarters in Vitez. However, I think it would have been a good thing had we clarified whose checkpoints these were and who stopped the UNPROFOR vehicles at the checkpoints and who stopped Colonel Stewart and Brigadier Cordy-Simpson at this checkpoint. Also, it was said that 20 houses were on fire in Busovaca. Whose houses are on fire? It would be a good thing to identify which houses are burning. Dzemo Merdan and Franjo Nakic had a joint commission, and we listened this, Enver Hadzihasanovic and I, and I believe that you have such reports among your documents too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, you had command over artillery in Central Bosnia, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That part of the artillery which the mixed artillery division had at its disposal at that time in Central Bosnia, yes, I had command over that. However, there was a part of the artillery attached to the brigades and the battalions, and this is not of a certain calibre but it existed in some companies as well. Now, depending upon which artillery you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let's read which artillery I am talking about, and if we could go into private session just briefly, for about ten lines, Mr. President, in some closed testimony?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go into private session for those ten lines then. (Private session) 19 [redacted] 20 [redacted] 21 [redacted] 22 [redacted] 23 [redacted] 24 [redacted] 25 [redacted]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We are now in open session. Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. Just going back, in response to the question of Judge Shahabuddeen, you do not know anybody who ordered the attack on Merdani and Grablje on the 25th, General, and is it also true that you do not know who sent the Vitezovi to Busovaca on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I wonder what the witness is saying. Is he saying that there was an attack but he didn't know who ordered the attack or is he saying he didn't know whether there was any attack?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understood that he didn't know if there was any attack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: That's what I thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think that's what I -- we understood the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General -- I will redirect my question. You noted that you didn't know if there was any attack on Merdani and Grablje on the 25th, and it is also true that you didn't know or don't know who ordered the Vitezovi to Busovaca on the 26th of January; is that statement accurate?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I remember, on the 25th, I just received information about a conflict at the checkpoint. The other information about the conflict was very scant, and I had no knowledge of an attack on Grablje and Merdani. I do not recall an order related to the Vitezovi either. I cannot recall whether it was an order from the command of the Vitezovi, why he went and what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us turn our attention to 456/8. Now, General, this is your order of 27 January, 1990, at 1740 hours, regarding the cessation of hostilities between the BiH and the HVO; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is right, and it was issued after the second meeting because the first meeting that we had on the 26th did not bear fruit and the BH army at that time implemented its activities in Lasva, Dusina, and Visnjica, and then Brigadier Cordy-Simpson convened a second meeting which was held on the 27th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, for report keeping purposes, the French copy as well as the original B/S/C copy has the time of this order accurately depicted as 1740. Unfortunately, the English copy that I see on the ELMO does not have that notation, and I just would ask at the appropriate time if the registrar could pen that in so the document can be as complete as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It seems that the French version doesn't bear the time of issuance of this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It does, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Where can you see it on the French version?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, can you help me? I can't find that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's right here, "1740 hours."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: In spite of this very sophisticated method, Mr. Prosecutor, I can't see it. I guess I must have a less sophisticated version of the document in my hands, Mr. Kehoe. Maybe you could cut your finger to put it on my document and show me. All right. It doesn't matter. You just have to tell us the time you have on your copy and that will be enough. Yes, it is the same document, but the time that appears on your document does in the appear on mine, so it will have to be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The English doesn't have it either, Judge. I thought it was on the French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. We can see the time on the B/C/S version, or can't we?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, this particular meeting, this cease-fire meeting, commenced at what time on the 27th of January?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Just a moment. Let me have a look, please. About 10.00 at the UNPROFOR headquarters for Bosnia-Herzegovina in Kiseljak, and the meeting was chaired by Brigadier Cordy-Simpson. At the meeting the following were present, the representatives of the 1st and 3rd Corps of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What time did you end that meeting, approximately?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. It lasted for quite some time. Immediately after the meeting, I started on the elaboration of this particular document. Perhaps it lasted until 1600, 1700. I can't confirm the exact time, because I didn't note the actual time when the meeting ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: At this particular point, General, would it be fair to say that you were operating from an office in the Kiseljak barracks?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know in what sense you mean "Operating." I was not able to operatively command units in Busovaca because I did not have any communication. So I didn't have my own office for me to be able to have my associates and to be operating. I used the office of the commander of the brigade, and I endeavoured to create the best possible conditions for my activities, but I did not have any operative way, and the problem of communication was highlighted previously as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The cease-fire order was supposed to take effect at what time?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 28th of January, 1993, 0001, that is to say, one minute after midnight.
